_doc: Trúc Thực Viên lineage (rules-proposals R5). Re-leaned Wood, Fire -> Wood, Water to its seat (place 25: Wood 33 %, Water 28 %, Fire 11 %). Outer gate: rain-on-bamboo-breath (Wood + Water, proposal). Inner gate and above: verdant-cycle-scripture (Wood, existing; a farmer's scripture: sow, root, mend, harvest). Secret arts: flooded-field-verse (inner, Water), sixty-year-flower (elders and head, Wood). Proposals are unpriced.

secret.note: taught to the head and the elders; never used while the grove stands

lineage.tree_route_note: The garden's bamboo and its seed fields: Bamboo Grove for the Verdant Cycle's Wood art speed, Seedling Field for the growth that the rain feeds.

techniques.name: Rain-on-Bamboo Breath (Trúc Vũ Tức)
techniques.concept: The garden's first method, breathed in the wet season standing among the culms with the rain running down them. Water qi is drawn in like rain into soil and pushed up node by node as Wood, the way a shoot rises after a storm. It is slow and cheap and never fails anyone, which is why the garden still teaches it to every field hand.

arts.new: Shoot After Rain (Vũ Hậu Xuân Duẩn)
arts.concept: For a few seconds after the holder is hit or healed by a Water art, her next Wood art comes out faster and lays one extra Wood stack.

arts.new: Bend, Not Break (Khuất Nhi Bất Chiết)
arts.concept: When a hit would take more than a fifth of her health, she bends: the hit is cut by a quarter.

techniques.lore: Written in 762 by the founder Ông Lục Tiết for the forty Wood disciples he led down from the palace, none of whom could hold the Feather Kindling. It is the first method the garden ever owned.

techniques.name: Flooded Field Verse (Thủy Điền Quyết)
techniques.concept: An irrigator's art turned to the fight. The holder floods the ground around her ankle-deep with qi water, as the garden floods its bamboo terraces in spring. A foe standing in the flood moves slowly and takes more from Wood arts, because the water feeds whatever grows out of it. The verse is sung while working the sluices, and the field hands know it as a work song before they know it as an art.

arts.concept: Floods a circle around the holder (a Field) for several seconds: while it is up, the foe is a fifth slower and takes more damage from Wood stacks.
Against a foe standing in the flood: roots their feet for one second and lays two Water stacks.

techniques.lore: Úy Thương Điền wrote it down in 1108, when she cut the first flood terraces below the grove. Before her the garden had no Water art at all, though half its hands were Water-rooted.

techniques.name: Sixty-Year Flower (Lục Thập Niên Hoa)
techniques.concept: The garden's last art, taken from the bamboo that flowers once in sixty years, seeds, and dies. The holder spends years storing Wood qi without using it, layer by layer, as a culm stores its strength. When she flowers, all of it is released in one bloom: she is healed and strengthened, and the foe is seeded with Wood stacks that ripen together. Afterwards her Wood is spent for a season, and an old cultivator who flowers may not recover.

arts.concept: Once per fight: releases all stored bloom; heals her by a share of her maximum health per stored layer and lays Wood stacks on the foe. Her Wood arts are then sealed for the rest of the fight.
A stance: while she uses no Wood art, she gains one stored bloom layer every few seconds and a little defense.

techniques.lore: Written by the second head Tất Mạn Thu after the flowering of 990, when she watched the whole grove bloom and die in a month. Ninh Trúc Thực learned it in 1040 and has never used it. In the garden it is said that a head who flowers does not see the next spring.
